picks.t: Noah Kahan – The Great Divide Tour
picks.d: Noah Kahan brings his folk-indie heartbreak anthems to Oracle Park for one massive night — expect 'Dial Drunk,' 'Northern Attitude,' and a crowd that knows every single word. Support comes from Gigi Perez and Annabelle Dinda, so get there early. Tickets are face-value protected via Ticketmaster's Exchange, so what you see is what you pay.

picks.t: Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc — SFMOMA Opening
picks.d: SFMOMA debuts a monumental site-specific installation weaving painting, video projection, and sound into an immersive meditation on time and nature — and the best part? It's in the admission-free gallery on Floor 1. This is a genuine opening-week moment at one of the city's best museums. Walk in, look up, and be transported.

Muse is one of the greatest live bands on the planet, full stop — lasers, pyro, Matthew Bellamy hitting notes no human should hit, and a concept album about alien radio signals to tie it all together. Shoreline is the perfect outdoor amphitheater for this kind of cinematic rock spectacle. One-night-only, so don't sleep on it.

Classic cars, food trucks, live entertainment, and local vendors take over the Lower Fillmore for one of summer's most feel-good free street events. It runs right into prime Friday-night energy, so grab a bite from the trucks and then drift into whatever evening you've planned. Zero dollars in, maximum vibes out.

picks.t: Daniel Caesar – Son of Spergy Tour
picks.d: Daniel Caesar's silky R&B hits Chase Center on Friday for night two of his SF run, with 070 Shake along for the ride — his new album debuted at #4 on the Billboard 200 and #1 on the R&B chart, so this setlist is going to be stacked. 'Get You,' 'Best Part,' and a whole lot of new heat. One night left to catch him.

Salesforce Park turns eight and celebrates with a three-day rooftop music and food festival in the heart of downtown — live music, DJs, drinks, and some of the best people-watching in the city, all suspended above the Embarcadero. It's a rare multi-day outdoor hang that's genuinely easy to drop into on any of the three days.

picks.t: Courtney Barnett – Creature of Habit Tour (3 Nights!)
picks.d: Courtney Barnett takes over the Fillmore for three nights with a genuinely special format: first set is instrumental music with collaborator Stella Mozgawa, second set is a deep dive through her full catalog from Sometimes I Sit and Think onward. This is the kind of intimate run that people talk about for years. Grab whichever night you can.

picks.t: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young Museum
picks.d: San Francisco is the ONLY U.S. city hosting this international blockbuster — 130 royal Egyptian treasures spanning 3,000 years, including gold jewelry and monumental granite statues that have never been seen in North America before. Timed entry means it's never overwhelming, and the de Young in Golden Gate Park is always a gorgeous day out.

picks.t: Train – Drops of Jupiter: 25 Years in the Atmosphere
picks.d: San Francisco's own Train celebrates 25 years of their iconic album with a full night of diamond-certified hits — 'Hey Soul Sister,' 'Drops of Jupiter,' 'Drive By' — all at Shoreline under the summer sky. Barenaked Ladies and Matt Nathanson open, so the whole evening is basically a nostalgia time machine with excellent acoustics.

Folsom Street transforms into a free block party with local food, pop-up vendors, art, DJs, live performances, and drag — the whole creative soul of SoMa in one stretch of pavement. It runs every fourth Thursday through September, but this week's is a great excuse to make a full Thursday night of it before heading to a show. Completely free.

picks.t: Damon Wayans at Punch Line Comedy Club
picks.d: A comedy legend at one of SF's legendary comedy rooms — Damon Wayans is bringing his stand-up to Punch Line and only 27 tickets remain, so this is very much a grab-them-now situation. Intimate venue, legendary performer, the kind of night you'll be referencing for years. Don't wait on this one.

The SF Standard is screening The Parent Trap outdoors and for free — bring a blanket, grab snacks, and enjoy peak late-summer vibes as the sun goes down over a park full of people who all know every line of this movie. It's the quintessential low-key Friday night and it costs exactly nothing.

SF Playhouse is putting on Hairspray all week with multiple showtimes — matinees, evening shows, the works — so there's genuinely no excuse not to fit it in. Big songs, big hair, big heart, and the kind of professional local theater that reminds you why the Playhouse has been a Union Square staple for years.

picks.t: Off the Grid Fort Mason: Friday Night Market
picks.d: The waterfront night market returns with food trucks, craft vendors, and live music as the sun sets over the bay — Fort Mason is one of those SF settings that never gets old, and on a clear August evening it's basically perfect. Free to enter, so you're only spending on the food, which is the right kind of math.

ongoing.t: Graciela Iturbide: Between Two Worlds — SFMOMA
ongoing.d: A stunning retrospective from the Mexico-based photographer, open daily through late fall at SFMOMA.

ongoing.t: The Etruscans: From the Heart of Ancient Italy — Legion of Honor
ongoing.d: Ancient Italian artifacts and treasures on view at the Legion of Honor through September 20.

ongoing.t: Civic Center Soundtrack — Free Lunchtime Concerts
ongoing.d: Live music at Fulton Plaza every Tuesday and Thursday noon–3 PM through October, totally free.

ongoing.t: This Asian American Life — Asian Art Museum
ongoing.d: Public art series exploring Chinatown life through the eyes of its mothers, workers, and children.

new.name: Mess Hall Food Hall
new.d: Three all-day concepts covering seafood, burgers, and Korean food, plus a full bar and grab-and-go picnic supplies for Tunnel Tops.

new.name: JouJou
new.d: Oysters, caviar, and champagne from the True Laurel and Lazy Bear team — this is the swanky splurge of the season.

new.name: Lucania
new.d: The A16 team brings Neapolitan pizza, house-made pasta, and stellar seafood to the Ferry Building's former MarketBar patio space.

new.name: Rize Up Bakery Café
new.d: Your favorite farmers market sourdough finally has a storefront — ube and sesame-scallion toasts plus great coffee in SoMa.

new.name: Bar Coto
new.d: Walk-in coffee, sandwiches, and some of the best summer gelato in the city from the beloved Cotogna team.

classic.name: Bix
classic.d: SF's most glamorous supper club — cocktails and duck confit in a Gold Rush-era alley, still impossibly cool after 35 years.

classic.name: City View Restaurant
classic.d: The best downtown dim sum, served from carts in a light-filled room above the Financial District — go early on weekends.

classic.name: La Taqueria
classic.d: The James Beard Award-winning burrito joint on Mission Street — no rice, just beans, meat, salsa, and decades of doing it right.

classic.name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
classic.d: Tomales Bay oysters shucked fresh at the Ferry Building or Wharf location — the Sweetwaters with mignonette are non-negotiable.

classic.name: Cotogna
classic.d: Wood-fired rustic Italian in the heart of North Beach — the roast chicken and house-made pasta are SF institutions.

bars.name: The DeLuxe
bars.d: The legendary Club Deluxe reborn with a better sound system, classic cocktails, and daily live music — the Haight's coolest new-old spot.

bars.name: True Laurel
bars.d: Produce-driven cocktails from the team behind Lazy Bear in a relaxed, beautiful Mission room — the menu changes constantly and it's always great.

bars.name: Toronado
bars.d: One of the great American beer bars — 50+ taps of serious craft and Belgian ales, zero pretension, perfect every time.

bars.name: Charmaine's (Proper Hotel)
bars.d: Sweeping rooftop views of the city skyline over well-made cocktails — the move for a warm August evening when you want to feel fancy without being stuffy.

bars.name: Quince Wine Room
bars.d: An intimate, encyclopedic wine list in one of SF's most beautiful historic neighborhoods — ideal for a slow, excellent Tuesday.

bars.name: Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar
bars.d: The Fairmont's legendary tiki bar with a floating bandstand on an indoor lagoon and mai tais strong enough to make you believe in magic.

bars.name: The Bearded Lady
bars.d: A welcoming, queer-friendly dive with cheap drinks, good company, and a Castro soul that feels like home in about 10 minutes.

bars.name: F8
bars.d: Two rooms of serious electronic music on Folsom Street — this week it's Matt Jereza's birthday takeover on Friday night, 10 PM to 3 AM.

games.detail: Giants return home after the Boston road series featuring new acquisition Rafael Devers
Middle of the homestand — great mid-week game night at the ballpark
Final Reds game before Arizona comes to town
New homestand kicks off against the D-backs — late-season Oracle Park at its best

sports.note: Giants sitting 4th in NL West — great late-summer games with Oracle Park's legendary bay views and zero playoff stress.

games.detail: Valkyries (25–9) on the road — watch on ION
Playoff-clinched Valkyries seek first-ever win vs. top-seeded Lynx — watch on USA Network
Third road game of the week for the hot Valkyries — watch on NBCS

sports.note: No home games this week but the Valkyries (2nd in West, 25–9) are must-watch TV with the playoffs locked in. Host a watch party!

concerts.d: The Great Divide Tour lands at Oracle Park with support from Gigi Perez and Annabelle Dinda. Kahan's folk-indie songwriting has turned him into one of the defining artists of his generation, and this is a proper stadium moment for him. Face-value tickets only via Ticketmaster Exchange.

Night two of Daniel Caesar's Chase Center run with 070 Shake in support. His new album Son of Spergy hit #1 on the R&B chart, so expect a setlist that balances deep cuts with the hits that made him a household name. Smooth, soulful, and genuinely moving live.

The former YSL Records rapper plays the Fillmore in support of his 2026 album Emotions, riding the buzz from his appearances on Kanye's Bully earlier this year. The Fillmore is one of the best rooms in the country for hip-hop — expect an intense, electric set.

A diverse multi-act bill at the Fillmore pairing Tropidelic's reggae-rock-funk fusion with hip-hop and alt sounds from Little Stranger and Jarv. This is the kind of eclectic Fillmore night that SF does better than anywhere else — show up not knowing everything and leave a fan.

San Francisco's hometown heroes celebrate the 25th anniversary of Drops of Jupiter with a full outdoor show at Shoreline, joined by Barenaked Ladies and Matt Nathanson. Three platinum-certified bands on one bill under the summer sky — this is a legitimately great value evening.

Three-night Fillmore run with a beautifully structured show: an instrumental first set with Stella Mozgawa, then a deep catalog dive through four albums of essential indie rock. This format is rare and the room is intimate — exactly the kind of experience that doesn't come around often.

The Wow! Signal Tour is built around an album inspired by a 1977 alien radio signal — which is exactly the level of ambition you want from a Muse concept tour. Spectacular production, massive sound, and a setlist that will absolutely wreck you in the best way. One night only at Shoreline.

concertsOngoing.t: San Francisco Symphony – Rachmaninoff Piano Concerto No. 2
concertsOngoing.d: Davies Symphony Hall presents Rachmaninoff's beloved concerto — check sfsymphony.org for exact Aug 21–27 dates and remaining seats.

singles.t: Matt Jereza's Birthday Takeover at F8
singles.d: Two rooms, two very different dancefloors — front room brings global club, hip-hop, baile funk, and Miami bass, while the back room goes deep into house, techno, and hyperpop. It's a stacked guest lineup curated by one of SF's best DJs, and the birthday energy means the crowd is going to be there to have a genuinely great time. 21+.

Meet 8–12 local singles in one structured, low-pressure evening at Blackbird — the format means you're never stuck in an awkward conversation for more than a few minutes, and the energy in these rooms is genuinely fun. SF's most popular speed dating series runs multiple age brackets weekly, so there's a slot for everyone.

The younger-skewing bracket at Blackbird is a great early-evening event that frees you up for a full night afterward — meet 8–12 singles, see who you click with, and then make plans accordingly. The format is genuinely low-stakes and the venue is comfortable and unpretentious.

A free outdoor block party on Folsom Street with DJs, drag performances, local vendors, food, and a crowd that's there to have a good time — this is genuinely one of the best free ways to meet people in the city right now. The SoMa creative community shows up in force, the vibe is welcoming and festive, and it costs absolutely nothing to walk in.

A three-day rooftop festival celebrating Salesforce Park's 8th birthday — music, DJs, food, and drinks above downtown SF with a crowd that's naturally social and in a good mood. Drop in on any day or all three, and the open rooftop setting makes it easy and natural to strike up a conversation. One of the best low-pressure socializing settings of the week.

singles.t: Monet X Change at Cobb's Comedy Club
singles.d: The RuPaul's Drag Race star brings her sharp, theatrical stand-up to Cobb's for a double-header Friday night — comedy shows are genuinely one of the best date or meetup formats because the shared laughs do all the social heavy lifting for you. Two show times means you can plan around dinner either before or after. 18+.

singlesOngoing.d: Coed volleyball, pickleball, kickball, and more — great recurring leagues for meeting people through activity rather than awkward small talk.

singlesOngoing.t: Run Club SF & SF Front Runners — Weekly Group Runs
singlesOngoing.d: Free weekly group runs through Golden Gate Park and the Presidio — the social club with a running problem, open to all levels.

date.title: Sunset, Stars & No Cover
date.tagline: The perfect Friday night that costs basically nothing

steps.title: Fillmore Hot August Night
steps.detail: Start at the Lower Fillmore street festival — classic cars, live music, food trucks, and a golden-hour energy that's genuinely hard to beat. It's free and it's festive.

steps.title: Food Truck Dinner
steps.detail: Grab dinner together from the food trucks at the street festival — walk around, share bites, and pick your favorites. This is the low-pressure version of a dinner date.

steps.title: Stroll to Off the Grid, Fort Mason
steps.detail: Head up to Fort Mason for the Friday Night Market — waterfront views, more vendors, live music, and that perfect late-summer SF evening light. Free entry, no agenda.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Sunset Walk
steps.detail: End the night with a walk — or find a park bench with a view and just talk. August evenings in SF are rare and warm. Make the most of it.

date.title: Art, Oysters & Courtney Barnett
date.tagline: Culture, great food, and an unforgettable show

steps.title: Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc at SFMOMA
steps.detail: Start the evening at SFMOMA's admission-free ground floor gallery for the brand-new Jacob Hashimoto installation — immersive, beautiful, and free. This is the kind of thing that sparks real conversation.

steps.title: Oysters at Hog Island, Ferry Building
steps.detail: Walk to the Ferry Building for Tomales Bay oysters and whatever wine you're feeling. Keep it light and save room — Embarcadero views included.

steps.title: Drinks at Bar Coto
steps.detail: A quick stop at the Cotogna team's new walk-in Jackson Square bar for gelato or a pre-show drink — it's a beautiful new space and genuinely delightful.

steps.title: Courtney Barnett at The Fillmore
steps.detail: Head to the Fillmore for the Creature of Habit Tour — instrumental first set, deep catalog second set. One of the most thoughtfully constructed shows of the year in one of the world's greatest rooms.

date.title: JouJou, Pharaohs & Muse
date.tagline: A full sensory blowout from champagne to pyro

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young Museum
steps.detail: Start your afternoon at the de Young with the U.S.-exclusive Egyptian exhibition — 130 royal treasures spanning 3,000 years, including gold jewelry and granite statues never before seen in North America. Timed entry, so book ahead.

steps.title: JouJou for Dinner
steps.detail: The splurge dinner of the season — oysters, caviar, champagne, and impeccable French seafood from the True Laurel and Lazy Bear team at their new Design District restaurant. Dress up a little.

steps.title: Charmaine's Rooftop for a Nightcap
steps.detail: Head to the Proper Hotel rooftop for a cocktail with city skyline views — the perfect transition from dinner to the drive down to Shoreline.

steps.title: Muse – The Wow! Signal Tour at Shoreline
steps.detail: One of the greatest live rock spectacles on earth, performing a concept album about alien intelligence under the open Shoreline sky. Lasers, pyro, anthems. This is why you come to shows.

solo.title: Museum Morning, Free Beats
solo.tagline: Fill your brain and your ears without spending a dime

steps.title: Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc — SFMOMA
steps.detail: The admission-free ground floor gallery just opened its newest major installation this week — give yourself a full hour to sit with it. Immersive solo museum time hits differently than going with a crowd.

steps.title: Civic Center Soundtrack Free Concert
steps.detail: Walk to Fulton Plaza for the free lunchtime concert series — live music, fresh air, and people-watching from noon to 3 PM every Tuesday and Thursday. Bring lunch from a nearby spot.

steps.title: Asian Art Museum: This Asian American Life
steps.detail: The Asian Art Museum is free on the first Sunday of the month, but worth full admission any day — especially for the current public art series exploring Chinatown life through a child's perspective.

solo.title: Ballpark, Beers & Baseball
solo.tagline: The classic SF solo Monday done right

steps.title: Bar Coto for Pre-Game Gelato
steps.detail: The Cotogna team's new Jackson Square all-day café is walk-in only and perfect for a quick solo stop — coffee or a drink and excellent gelato before heading south.

steps.title: Giants vs. Cincinnati Reds — Oracle Park
steps.detail: Grab a single seat and settle in for the homestand opener on Monday, August 24. Late-season games have a relaxed energy — great views of the bay, garlic fries in hand, no pressure.

steps.title: Toronado for a Nightcap
steps.detail: Lower Haight is a short ride from the park — Toronado's 50+ taps and zero pretension make it the ideal solo wind-down. Pick something Belgian and call it a perfect evening.

solo.title: Pharaohs, Lucania & Muse
solo.tagline: A full solo culture day ending in a rock spectacle

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young
steps.detail: Book your timed entry and spend the morning with 3,000 years of Egyptian royal history. San Francisco is the only U.S. city hosting this — take your time, read the panels, let it land.

steps.title: Lunch at Lucania — Ferry Building
steps.detail: Roasted sardines, house pasta, and a glass of Sicilian white on the Embarcadero patio at the A16 team's new Ferry Building restaurant. Solo lunch at a beautiful waterfront spot is deeply underrated.

steps.title: Wander the Ferry Building Marketplace
steps.detail: Walk off lunch through the Ferry Building's artisan stalls — local cheese, olive oil, craft chocolate. Pick up a snack for the show later.

steps.title: Muse at Shoreline Amphitheatre
steps.detail: Drive down to Mountain View for The Wow! Signal Tour. Solo shows at Shoreline are underrated — you can find the perfect spot on the lawn, no one's waiting on you, and Muse will absolutely take care of the rest.

birthday.title: Rooftop Birthday Kickoff
birthday.tagline: Start the birthday weekend high above the city — free to enter

steps.title: Off the Grid Fort Mason Friday Night Market
steps.detail: Kick off the birthday weekend at Fort Mason's waterfront night market — free entry, great food trucks, live music, and bay views as a built-in backdrop. Let the birthday person pick what they're eating.

steps.title: Rooftop Rhythms at Salesforce Park
steps.detail: Head downtown for the multi-day rooftop festival celebrating Salesforce Park's 8th birthday — there's something poetic about crashing a park's birthday party for your own. DJs, drinks, city views.

steps.title: Fillmore After Dark — Walk the Neighborhood
steps.detail: End the night in the Fillmore with the group's choice of bar — the strip is buzzing on Fridays. If the birthday person wants dancing, F8 on Folsom has Matt Jereza's takeover running until 3 AM.

birthday.title: Train, The Fillmore & Fort Mason
birthday.tagline: A classic SF birthday with a nostalgic soundtrack

steps.title: Off the Grid Fort Mason — Friday Dinner
steps.detail: Start the evening at the waterfront night market for dinner — everyone gets what they want, no reservation stress, and the setting is beautiful. Fort Mason is a birthday crowd pleaser.

steps.title: Drinks at Charmaine's Rooftop
steps.detail: Pre-show rooftop birthday drinks at the Proper Hotel with skyline views — toast to the birthday person properly before heading south.

steps.title: Train at Shoreline Amphitheatre
steps.detail: If the birthday is Wednesday, August 26 — or you can shift the plan — Train's 25th anniversary Drops of Jupiter show with Barenaked Ladies at Shoreline is a legitimately joyful, sing-along-all-night birthday show. From $42 per person.

birthday.title: Daniel Caesar, JouJou & Bottle Service
birthday.tagline: A full luxury birthday night the birthday person will not forget

steps.title: JouJou — Birthday Dinner
steps.detail: Reserve the whole experience — oysters, caviar, champagne flowing — at the hottest new restaurant of 2026. The True Laurel and Lazy Bear team do not miss. This is the dinner the birthday person deserves.

steps.title: Daniel Caesar at Chase Center
steps.detail: Head to Chase Center for Daniel Caesar's Friday night show — smooth R&B for a room full of people who love every song. Floor tickets or club-level for the birthday group.

steps.title: Matt Jereza's Birthday Takeover at F8
steps.detail: After the show, head to F8 for the birthday takeover — two rooms, stacked lineup, runs until 3 AM. It's someone else's birthday party and now it's yours too. The symmetry is perfect.

friends.title: Street Fest Friday Crawl
friends.tagline: Hit three free events in one Friday night without spending a dime on entry

steps.title: Fillmore Hot August Night
steps.detail: The crew meets at the Lower Fillmore street fest — classic cars, food trucks, free live entertainment. Get everyone fed and in the mood.

steps.title: Off the Grid Fort Mason Night Market
steps.detail: Walk or rideshare up to Fort Mason for the waterfront market. More food trucks, craft vendors, live music, and some of the best bay views in the city. Free entry.

steps.title: Sundown Cinema: The Parent Trap
steps.detail: Find the park screening for The Parent Trap — blankets out, someone brings snacks, everyone knows every line. The perfect end to a free-roaming Friday night with the group.

friends.title: Baseball, Beers & Comedy
friends.tagline: The ultimate SF squad Tuesday or Wednesday

steps.title: Pre-Game at Rize Up Bakery Café
steps.detail: Swing by the new Rize Up café in SoMa for coffee or a snack before the game — ube toast and sesame-scallion options for the adventurous ones in the group.

steps.title: Giants vs. Reds at Oracle Park
steps.detail: Grab a section of seats together for the homestand — Oracle Park garlic fries are non-negotiable. The Reds series runs Monday through Wednesday, so pick your night.

steps.title: Damon Wayans at Punch Line Comedy Club
steps.detail: After the game on Wednesday, head to the Punch Line for Damon Wayans — only 27 tickets left, so book NOW. The Financial District location is easy from the ballpark. End the night laughing.

friends.title: Muse, Mess Hall & Rooftop Views
friends.tagline: A full-day squad adventure ending in a rock spectacle

steps.title: Mess Hall Food Hall — The Presidio
steps.detail: The new Presidio food hall is perfect for a group lunch — everyone gets what they want, from seafood to Korean to burgers, with a full bar. Grab picnic supplies and spread out at Tunnel Tops afterward.

steps.title: Tunnel Tops Picnic — The Presidio
steps.detail: Golden Gate Bridge views, grass, and the best afternoon hang in the city. The Presidio is genuinely one of SF's greatest assets and August is the perfect time to be there.

steps.title: Charmaine's Rooftop Pre-Show Drinks
steps.detail: Head downtown for cocktails with city views before the drive south — get everyone in the right headspace for what's coming.

steps.title: Muse at Shoreline Amphitheatre
steps.detail: The Wow! Signal Tour at Shoreline — lawn tickets are affordable, the sound is enormous, and Muse is one of the best live bands you can see. A crew at a rock show on a warm August night. That's the whole thing.

parents.title: Park Picnic & A Movie
parents.tagline: Low-key, beautiful, and genuinely fun for all ages

steps.title: Mess Hall Food Hall — The Presidio
steps.detail: Easy, comfortable food hall lunch with something for everyone — the Presidio setting does half the work. Grab extra to-go for a picnic afterward.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young Museum
steps.detail: The de Young's blockbuster Egyptian exhibition is the kind of thing that impresses visiting parents effortlessly — monumental artifacts, gorgeous museum, Golden Gate Park setting. Book timed entry in advance.

steps.title: Japanese Tea Garden Stroll
steps.detail: Right next door to the de Young — a slow, beautiful walk through the oldest public Japanese garden in the U.S., with tea and fortune cookies at the tea house.

steps.title: Sundown Cinema: The Parent Trap
steps.detail: End the day at the free outdoor screening of The Parent Trap — blankets, snacks, and a movie the whole family actually loves. A genuinely lovely way to close out an SF day.

parents.title: Etruscans, Lucania & The Fillmore
parents.tagline: Culture, great Italian food, and a bit of rock and roll history

steps.title: The Etruscans — Legion of Honor
steps.detail: The Legion of Honor's Etruscan exhibition is a quieter, less-crowded alternative to the de Young blockbuster — equally fascinating and in one of SF's most beautiful museum buildings overlooking the Golden Gate.

steps.title: Lunch at Lucania — Ferry Building
steps.detail: The A16 team's new southern Italian restaurant at the Ferry Building is accessible and excellent — roasted sardines, pasta, and a patio with Embarcadero people-watching. Perfect for a leisurely parent lunch.

steps.title: Ferry Building Marketplace Walk
steps.detail: Let the parents browse the artisan stalls — Cowgirl Creamery cheese, Blue Bottle coffee, local olive oil. Easy, no-rush afternoon exploring.

steps.title: Courtney Barnett at The Fillmore
steps.detail: Take the parents to the Fillmore — it's a historic room with an incredible story, and Courtney Barnett's two-set format is genuinely sophisticated and impressive. This is the kind of show parents leave talking about.

parents.title: Pharaohs, JouJou & Train
parents.tagline: A proper SF blowout with something truly special at every turn

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young Museum
steps.detail: Start the day at the de Young with the U.S.-exclusive Egyptian blockbuster — 130 royal artifacts, timed entry, Golden Gate Park. This is the cultural highlight of the SF year and worth anchoring the whole visit around.

steps.title: Lunch at Hog Island — Ferry Building
steps.detail: Tomales Bay oysters and a seafood lunch on the Embarcadero — fresh, local, and a genuinely quintessential SF experience that out-of-town parents always love.

steps.title: Charmaine's Rooftop Cocktails
steps.detail: Pre-dinner drinks with the best skyline views in the city at the Proper Hotel. Give them the full panoramic SF moment before dinner.

steps.title: JouJou — Dinner
steps.detail: The splurge dinner of the season — oysters, champagne, impeccable French seafood from one of SF's most exciting new restaurant teams. This is the dinner worth flying in for.

steps.title: Train at Shoreline Amphitheatre (Wednesday only)
steps.detail: If the visit falls on Wednesday, August 26 — take the parents to see SF's own Train celebrate 25 years of Drops of Jupiter with Barenaked Ladies at Shoreline. Nostalgia, great sound, summer air. A perfect ending.
